newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 15.

text.p: The following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

State Secretary Murdiono says the final report by the official National Commission on Human Rights on the July 27 riots had left a number of things unclear and the government was still studying the case.

The head of the Indonesian Ulama Council (MUI), Hasan Basri, said the Islamic body regrets the burning and destruction of at least 25 churches in East Java last week. He said such acts were not in line with the Prophet's teachings.
Customs authorities in Bali found 29,295 tablets of the designer drug Ecstasy in two unclaimed suitcases which had been left unclaimed at the Ngurah Rai Airport for three months.
Influential MUI head Hasan Basri calls for a total ban on alcohol in Indonesia before exceptions are granted for the sale of alcoholic drinks.
The official National Commission on Human Rights has formed a team to investigate the attack on at least 25 churches in East Java last week.
At least 32 hotel projects in Jakarta are blocked because of delays in permission and problems with raising finance.
Rizal Ramli, leading economist from the Econit Advisory Group, says monetary contraction in 1996 will see the Indonesian economy cool down next year.
